summary: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a browser-based survival game for kids ages 7-12. Players manage a lunar outpost for 10 "sols" (days), making real engineering trade-offs between power, oxygen, and radiation shielding. Grounded in real NASA space weather data, every choice helps one system but costs another, teaching kids that deep space survival is all about balance.
details: Space-themed STEM content for kids often oversimplifies the engineering trade-offs of a real mission. I built this game to fix that. The player runs a lunar outpost and is faced with 10 dynamic events (solar flares, dusty solar panels, clogged air filters). They must balance Power, Oxygen, and Shielding. To make it educational, I didn't show the exact numbers until after a choice is made, players only see arrow hints. I also included a difficulty toggle (Easy, Normal, Hard) and a Mission Report at the end that compares their outpost to real NASA mission types (e.g., "Research Station" vs "Tech Demo"). The game is fully accessible, mobile-responsive, and features a glossary to explain terms like "regolith" and "sol."
